title: Cap. III Rat. 7: mere good pleasure would elect all equally disposed — Valentia
pass_a_gloss: Reason 7. If God should predestine to glory from the mere good pleasure of his will, and not from foresight of works, then he would predestine all equally, because all are equally disposed to receive that gift. For if God does not elect men inasmuch as they are foreseen as well-working, and persevering in good works, it follows that they are elected inasmuch as they are foreknown to be men, or sinners: but this belongs to all; therefore all would be elected. This argument is found in Gregory of Valencia, On 1. q. 23.
pass_b_english: Rat. 7. If God predestined to glory from the mere good pleasure of his will and not from foresight of works, then he would predestine all alike, because all are equally disposed to receive that gift. For if he does not elect people as foreseen working well and persevering in good works, they must be elected as foreknown to be human beings or sinners — which belongs to all; so all would be elected. So argues Gregory of Valencia (In 1. q. 23).
source_text: Rat. 7. Si Deus praedestinaret ad gloriam ex mero beneplacito voluntatis suae, et non ex praevisione operum, tum omnes ex aequo praedestinaret, quia omnes aeque dispositi sunt ad illud donum recipiendum. Nam si Deus non eligat homines quatenus praevidentur ut bene operantes, et in bonis operibus perseverantes, consequens est ut eligantur quatenus praesciuntur esse homines, vel peccatores: at hoc omnibus convenit; omnes ergo eligerentur. Habetur hoc argumentum apud Gregorium de Valentia, In 1. qu. 23.
